newsitem.title: UK: Ex-BET boss wins huge payoff from UK's Rentokil.
newsitem.headline: Ex-BET boss wins huge payoff from UK's Rentokil.

text.p: A high-flying boss who rescued business services group BET from the doldrums only to be sacked after its takeover this year by Rentokil won three million pounds ($4.5 billion) in compensation on Wednesday.
The award to U.S.-born John Clark, 55, by a High Court judge was thought to be a British record. It was four times the amount offered as a pre-trial settlement but only half of what Clark had sought.
Rentokil, the pest control to security group which recently changed its name to Rentokil Initial Plc, immediately said it would appeal against the ruling.
A Rentokil spokesman said it was "an absolutely enormous sum of money, and clearly we are going to appeal."
Clark alleged that Rentokil had wrongfully dismissed him after its hostile takeover of BET plc in April.
"I am very pleased with the outcome," Clark told reporters. "The sums recovered represent what the court has held to be the strict entitlement under my contract and no more."
"I regret it was necessary to bring my claim to court. I normally seek to resolve such matters in a private and mature manner."
Clark, described by the judge as "an extremely able, energetic and successful businessman", was recruited by BET in 1991.
He transformed the group's fortunes but was ousted after Rentokil gained majority control of BET after spending 2.2 billion pounds ($3.50 billion) in a hostile takeover bid.
Clark told reporters he was now eager to continue his search for a position as chief executive in a major organisation.
